title: Bash command history
whyItMatters: Every command typed in a bash shell is saved here, including server names, paths, passwords typed by mistake and what the person was working on.
source: GNU Bash manual, HISTFILE: the default history file is ~/.bash_history: https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Bash-Variables.html
notes: bash writes the file when the shell exits, so the newest commands may be missing while a terminal is open. HISTFILE, HISTSIZE and HISTIGNORE in .bashrc can change what is kept or where.

steps: Close all open terminal windows so the shell does not write history on exit.
Delete the file named in the plan using your file manager.
cleanup.risk: Deletes your command recall history in Bash. Past commands and any credentials typed into the shell will be lost.
